verdicts.title: Make __repr__ actually round-trippable (kwargs form, quoted values) instead of documenting a format it never produced
verdicts.issues: Verified: befores verbatim (bittype.py 254-264, int.py anchor 610-617; exact-match patch applied cleanly); patched-copy probes all pass: eval(repr(x), {name: cls}) round-trips type/bits/endianness/value for UInt6/8/16/64, SInt8 both formats, SInt7 ones_complement, Float16 1.5/NaN/-0.0/inf/-inf (NaN bits exact, -0.0 sign kept), UTF8Stringx8 with quotes+non-ASCII in the value, Bufferx2, little-endian boxes, and specialize()d anonymous classes; str() unchanged; Struct repr ('Row(gid=64, v=-3)') and bound-field repr unaffected; no repo/test/oracle dependency on the old repr format (grep of repr(/!r across package and tests; _legacy_aggregate.py has zero repr/!r usage; only repr assertions in tests are BitVector/Struct/bound-field, all still green). Full suite on the patched copy: 854/854, suite confirmed importing the work-copy package. Compose check with narrowing-3's _StructPackedSInt applied on the same copy: SInt8.__repr__ still resolves to SInt.__repr__ (neither _StructPackedSInt nor StructPackedBitType defines __repr__), repr carries int_format, and eval round-trips bits+format+value (SInt8(-5, 'signed_magnitude') -> -5 sign-magnitude, not tc -123) for all four standard widths; combined copy also 854/854. Notebook-staleness risk note verified accurate (conversions.ipynb x2 and binder.ipynb contain old-format outputs). NITS (not blocking): (1) proposed test #3 prose is numerically garbled - 'eval'd signed_magnitude repr has value -123, not the twos_complement -117' matches no possible bit pattern (bits 10000101: tc=-123, sm=-5; -117 fits nothing); fix the numbers before pinning that test. (2) specialize() without name_ yields __name__ '_UInt'/'_SInt', so repr shows a class name importable from nowhere - the docstring's 'with the class name in scope' wording keeps the promise honest and eval works once the user binds it, but the maintainer should know anonymous-class reprs are only round-trippable with a manual binding. (3) UInt64 repr is ~97 chars (bits-form is verbose at wide widths) - deliberate, designer already weighed vs str(). PRE-EXISTING: SInt8(bits='10000101', int_format='signed_magnitude').value reads -123 pre-narrowing-3 (struct unpack ignores instance int_format at standard widths) - that is the already-filed narrowing finding; the new repr faithfully preserves (does not cause or worsen) it.

verdicts.title: Document to_pyint's real receiver instead of a phantom `bitstring` parameter
verdicts.issues: Verified: before verbatim (int.py 76-89; also byte-identical to the docstring extracted from the 4-weeks-ago reference pyc, confirming both the pre-existing defect and that the dash-list Parameters/Returns style the rewrite preserves is the reference-era style). Every documented claim runtime-checked on the patched copy: Int.to_pyint('1010') == -6 (unbound '01'-string call, signed defaults True), Int.to_pyint('1010', signed=False) == 10, Int.to_pyint(BitVector('1010'), signed=False) == 10, SInt8(-5).to_pyint() == -5, UInt8(200).to_pyint() == 200 (is_signed=False honored); the 'module itself calls it unbound' rationale matches int.py:596. The 'Default is self.is_signed where that exists' wording matches the getattr(self, 'is_signed', True) code, and the missing-colon typo after '(Optional[bool], optional)' is fixed. No patched line over 88 columns; 854/854. No issues.

verdicts.title: Point the SInt docstring at SignedConfig, the class that actually exists
verdicts.issues: Verified: both before fragments verbatim (int.py 545-547 and 561-562, including the unclosed-quote typo); after the patch SInt.__doc__ contains 'SignedConfig' exactly twice, '`Config`' is gone, 'Default is "twos_complement".' is properly closed, bytemaker.bittypes.int.SignedConfig exists and matches what __init__ reads, no line over 88 columns, 854/854. Region disjoint from narrowing-6's Int-docstring edits as claimed. Minor scope note (not a problem): the fix also repairs the adjacent quote typo, which is beyond the finding's literal ask but flagged honestly in the fix text and clearly beneficial. No issues.

verdicts.title: Add __all__ to fields.pyi so the checker's star-import surface matches runtime
verdicts.issues: Verified empirically with mypy 2.3.0 (--follow-imports=silent to isolate the probe from the package's many pre-existing internal mypy errors): BEFORE (pristine stub) the probe (star-import + annotations u8/f32/u1/s63 + direct u17 import) checks clean - u1/s63 wrongly accepted; AFTER exactly the two claimed name-defined errors ('Name "u1" is not defined; did you mean "u16" or "u17"?' and 'Name "s63" is not defined'), while u8/f32 via star and directly-imported u17 stay accepted. Runtime unchanged: star-import still binds exactly the 11 names, direct imports of u1/u17 still work. Stub __all__ parsed via ast equals bytemaker.fields.__all__ (same 11 names, same order, no typos, no missing public name). Before-text verbatim at fields.pyi 14-16; no line over 88 columns; 854/854. One caveat for the maintainer: a bare 'python -m mypy' over this repo drowns in roughly a hundred pre-existing package-internal errors, so the clean before/after story - and the proposed mypy-based CI test - implicitly require an isolated probe invocation (e.g. --follow-imports=silent); the test description should say so.

verdicts.title: SInt.value setter's 'reject out-of-range' claim: resolved by narrowing-3's per-instance gate (no new edit)
verdicts.issues: Verified both halves empirically. Current repo: SInt8(0, int_format='signed_magnitude'); s.value = 200 -> silently -56 (comment's claim false; repro matches the finding). With narrowing-3 applied to the work copy: the same store raises ValueError('Value out of range for the specified bit_length for sign-magnitude notation.') exactly as claimed; in-range sm stores work (bits 10000101), tc SInt8 still wraps 200 -> -56, and SInt16/32/64 sm out-of-range stores raise too; combined suite 854/854. The quoted before-text (598-613) is verbatim, and narrowing-2's accepted setter rewrite does keep the 'reject out-of-range values' sentence, so the deferral is coherent with the accepted narrowing set. The contingent fallback comment is factually accurate for the pre-narrowing-3 world. NIT: the fallback could be maximally precise by saying the pre-3 gate reads the GLOBAL SignedConfig rather than this instance's int_format ('under the default global config' covers it, but names the symptom not the mechanism); moot while narrowing-3 stands. Since this solution proposes no edit, nothing to break.
